title: Carina Biotech - Dedicated capacity qualification
summary: Initial qualification for reserved GPU capacity for Carina Biotech's inference workloads. Focus on isolation requirements, burst model, pre-warm strategy, security (KMS/SSO/SOC2) and scaling expectations. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot evaluation with a bench of synthetic burst tests and to share security/compliance pack.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-17
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samira (Redwood), Ethan (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (CTO, Carina), Marco Silva (Infra), Jin Park (Security)
Links referenced: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/dedicated-overview (shared), security-pack link (sent after call)

Auto-summary (auto-transcribed, may be fuzzy): Discussed reserved GPUs, isolation options (VPC vs on-prem), burst behavior, pre-warm/hotpool and fallback routing. Security checks: KMS, SSO, SOC 2. Agreed on pilot + deliverables.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for making time. i'm Samira from Redwood, and with me is Ethan from our solutions team. quick round?
[00:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: hi, lena here. quick background, we're a clinical research platform, inference is powering patient triage and summary generation, very latency sensitive and needs strict data controls.
[00:28] Marco: marco, infra lead — i manage the kubernetes clusters and how we route to cloud endpoints.
[00:36] Jin Park: jin, security engineer — focused on encryption keys, audit trails, and whether PHI can leave our VPC.
[00:44] Ethan: great, to set expectations we'll cover architecture options (hosted, dedicated, private), how reserved capacity works, and then surface any blockers for a pilot.
[00:57] Dr. Lena: perfect. quick question up front — we want deterministic tail latency for patient-facing flows. what SLAs do you typically hit for dedicated pools?
[01:10] Samira: for dedicated we target p95 under the model's expected seq len, usually 150-200ms for medium sized open models on an A100 style pool — your mileage varies by model and token length. we can run benchmarks with your payload to be exact.
[01:26] Marco: is that with batching enabled? our current traf is spiky with bursts during clinical review windows.
[01:34] Ethan: yes that's with our continuous batching tuned to meet latency SLOs. for spikes we offer warm-hotpool pre-warm options and a burst guard that can route to a higher-cost warm pool or fallback hosted variant.
[01:49] Jin: clarify the warm pool — is the warm pool shared multi-tenant or isolated per customer? we need strict tenant isolation for PHI.
[01:58] Samira: good call. we have two flavors: reserved dedicated pools which are tenant-isolated (physical GPU allocation), and warm pools which can be either isolated for dedicated customers or shared for cost efficiency depending on contract. for PHI you'd pick an isolated warm pool or full private deployment.
[02:18] Marco: ok. what's the difference operationally between "dedicated isolated warm pool" and "private on-prem"?
[02:25] Ethan: operationally private means you run a Redwood private control plane and can keep inference inside your VPC or on-prem hardware — full network/infra control. dedicated isolated pools are still managed by Redwood but we guarantee tenancy separation and no noisy neighbor at the GPU level. private is heavier lift but gives max control and data never leaves network perimeter.
[02:46] Dr. Lena: security is big — Jin can you list our must-haves?
[02:50] Jin: sure — KMS integration for keys, SSO for console access (SAML), audit logs with immutable retention, and SOC 2 reports. also need to know data at rest encryption for any transient caching (KV-cache) and ability to disable logging for PHI endpoints.
[03:10] Ethan: we integrate with customer KMS/HSM, support SAML SSO, and can configure audit log retention. KV cache can be encrypted and scoped; we also support per-route opt-outs for caching. i'll share specifics in the security pack.
[03:25] Marco: concrete question on burst sizing — our peak windows hit ~1800 requests/min with average tokens per request about 600, w/ short spikes to 4500 rpm for 5-10 minutes. we need to model both sustained and burst costs.
[03:45] Samira: that's really useful. can you also share concurrency and latency targets? for example p95 < 500ms during spikes?
[03:53] Marco: target p95 400ms, p99 under 1.2s during worst-case.
[04:02] Ethan: ok. for that sort of pattern we'd normally recommend a baseline reserved pool sized for steady-state plus a hot pre-warmed pool sized to absorb short spikes. our model of prewarm uses small warm instances kept with KV cache primed to avoid cold-start KV hits. for extreme spikes we can overflow to hosted fallbacks or spin up burst capacity if commercial terms allow.
[04:25] Jin: spin up — how fast? we can't have 10s of seconds stall on an SLA-critical flow.
[04:31] Ethan: warm pools are immediate. cold starts take a few minutes depending on image size; our hotpool pre-warm avoids that. fallback to hosted is immediate in routing but may change cost and data residency constraints.
[04:45] Dr. Lena: fallback to hosted — that worries us because of PHI. is there an encrypted-only path or redaction option?
[04:53] Samira: yes two options — 1) route only non-PHI payloads to hosted; 2) use private VPC endpoints for dedicated (keeps data in your VPC) or 3) use on-prem private deployment. we can also propose a proxy that strips identifiers before sending to hosted.
[05:12] Marco: ok, for now we want a pilot that keeps everything in dedicated isolated pools — no hosted fallback enabled. but we want to test failover behavior in a staging environment with synthetic redacted traffic.
[05:23] Ethan: reasonable. we'll configure pilot constraints accordingly.
[05:27] Samira: commercial question — are you looking for a long-term commit or a PO-led pilot?
[05:33] Dr. Lena: initial pilot, 2 weeks, then evaluate cost and then commit to a 12-month reserved agreement if it meets SLOs.
[05:41] Samira: that's aligned with our standard progression. we'll send a pilot term sheet and then a renewal pricing model for 12 months.
[05:49] Jin: encryption — for KV cache is encryption at rest sufficient or do you support in-use encryption?
[05:55] Ethan: in-use encryption (TEE) isn't out-of-the-box for all models; we offer KMS/HSM for key management and disk-based encryption for caches. we can discuss specialized TEE options with our security team if needed.
[06:12] Marco: curious about autoscaling: if we provision reserved GPUs, can we autoscale additional non-reserved nodes for burst? how are costs tracked back to us?
[06:22] Samira: yes you can have hybrid autoscaling: reserved baseline + on-demand burst capacity. costs for burst are metered separately and visible in the console with token-level breakdowns. we'll show you the console during the pilot.
[06:36] Ethan: one thing to note: for predictable p95 you want the burst policy to pre-warm in anticipation where possible — we can use schedule-based pre-warm if your spikes are predictable (like daily review windows) or we can use reactive warmup that trades a bit more cost for responsiveness.
[06:55] Dr. Lena: our spikes are partially predictable — eod runs and clinical review times. schedule-based prewarm seems promising.
[07:04] Marco: what about tenant fencing? if we run multiple models for different product lines, can we pin models to specific GPU sets?
[07:11] Ethan: yes model pinning is supported — you can pin a model version to a GPU subset. that helps reduce eviction and cold-starts for critical models.
[07:21] Jin: audit logs — we need immutable retention for 13 months. can that be configured per-customer?
[07:27] Samira: yes retention windows are configurable (enterprise add-on). we'll include the policy options in the security pack.
[07:35] Dr. Lena: question on quantization — we use quantized models in prod for cost. any limit on quantized model support?
[07:42] Ethan: our runtime supports common quantized formats; the runtime will pick kernels accordingly. some extreme quant formats may need validation but generally supported.
[07:52] Marco: benchmarks — we want you to run our model with our token distribution. what's needed from us?
[07:58] Ethan: ideally a sanitized sample trace with request sizes, concurrency over time, and a small model artifact or pointer to the model repo. if you can't share model, then run a local load generator with our sample traffic template. i'll send the template.
[08:12] Samira: okay let's talk pricing briefly — pilot pricing is usually a reduced reserved rate plus burst metering. after pilot we can propose a 12-month reserved commitment with predictable unit economics.
[08:23] Dr. Lena: one more procurement Q — our security team will want SOC2 + penetration test attestation. is that available?
[08:30] Samira: yes we have SOC 2 Type II and pen test summaries we can share under NDA. we'll send the pack post-call.
[08:38] Jin: good. also need to confirm KMS key rotation policies and if Redwood rotates keys or we keep control.
[08:45] Ethan: keys live in customer KMS if you want full control; Redwood can use customer KMS for encryption keys so you manage rotation.
[08:54] Marco: operational runbooks — we'd like escalation paths and an SLO for failover when capacity is exhausted.
[09:01] Samira: we provide an ops playbook, runbooks for failover, and a 24/7 on-call for enterprise SLAs. the SLOs and escalation will be part of the dedicated contract.
[09:12] Dr. Lena: any known noisy-neighbor mitigation strategies?
[09:16] Ethan: for dedicated you get physical GPU isolation. for shared warmpools we have tenant throttles, but for PHI use-cases we recommend isolated GPUs.
[09:27] Marco: will the pilot require network peering or can it go over secure internet endpoints?
[09:33] Samira: for dedicated isolated pools we can use VPC peering or private link; secure internet endpoints are possible but peering is preferred for predictable latency.
[09:43] Dr. Lena: timeline — we want pilot to start before year-end if possible. feasible?
[09:48] Samira: yes, if paperwork and NDA are quick we can spin a pilot in 5-7 business days for a limited pool.
[09:56] Marco: what telemetry will you expose during pilot?
[09:59] Ethan: token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, per-model qps, and GPU utilization. we'll give dashboard access and a short walkthrough.
[10:12] Jin: ask on data residency — are logs ever replicated outside the region?
[10:16] Samira: logs live in region by default, replication only with explicit consent. we'll note that in security pack.
[10:23] Dr. Lena: ok that's helpful. any red flags on your side?
[10:27] Ethan: none yet. the main ops item is making sure the traffic profile for the bench is accurate so we size pre-warm correctly.
[10:36] Samira: to wrap, action items: ethan will send burst template, i will send pilot term sheet and pricing, jin will send compliance wishlist. we schedule pilot kickoff next week.
[10:48] Dr. Lena: sounds good. one small point — we've been exploring on-prem GPU for regulated models. will Redwood support hybrid where some models stay on-prem and others hit dedicated?
[10:58] Ethan: yes hybrid is a supported pattern — model routing by policy, pinning, and fallbacks possible. routing policies can be region, model, or route-based.
[11:10] Marco: last ops note — how do you handle model upgrades and KV cache invalidation? we need predictable rollout windows.
[11:18] Samira: rollouts support canary and A/B. KV cache invalidation can be configured per rollout, we also support a cache drain window to avoid tail regressions.
[11:28] Jin: ok thanks everyone.
[11:31] Samira: thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack and schedule.

End of transcript.
